name: eng-2176-obsidian
title: Escape regex metacharacters in discourse node format expressions (Obsidian)

prepare.why: the vault has a proof database session, so sync writes to the proof database
sync mode is on, so Sync discourse nodes to Supabase runs

apply.js: (async () => { const plugin = proof.obsidian.plugin(); plugin.settings.syncModeEnabled = true; await plugin.saveSettings(); })()

prepare.why: a Draft Claim node type whose format has parentheses, and a note in it with a fixed node id

apply.js:
(async () => { await proof.obsidian.closeModals(); const plugin = proof.obsidian.plugin(); const now = Date.now(); if (!proof.obsidian.nodeType('Draft Claim')) { plugin.settings.nodeTypes.push({ id: 'pk-2176-draft-claim', name: 'Draft Claim', format: 'Claim (draft) - {content}', color: '#8B5CF6', created: now, modified: now }); await plugin.saveSettings(); } await proof.obsidian.write('Claim (draft) - Sleep improves memory.md', '---
nodeTypeId: pk-2176-draft-claim
nodeInstanceId: pk-2176-draft-claim-note
---
A Draft Claim note.
'); })()

prepare.why: no Draft Claim note from an earlier run's Create discourse node
a note of the vault's default Claim type

apply.js:
(async () => { const claim = proof.obsidian.nodeType('Claim'); if (!claim) throw new Error('The vault has no Claim type.'); await proof.obsidian.write('CLM - PK 2176 default claim.md', '---
nodeTypeId: ' + claim.id + '
---
A default Claim note.
'); })()

prepare.why: a node type whose format has a placeholder but no {content}, the way an import can create one, and a note in it

apply.js:
(async () => { const plugin = proof.obsidian.plugin(); const now = Date.now(); if (!proof.obsidian.nodeType('PK No Content')) { plugin.settings.nodeTypes.push({ id: 'pk-2176-no-content', name: 'PK No Content', format: 'NCT - {question}', color: '#0EA5E9', created: now, modified: now }); await plugin.saveSettings(); } await proof.obsidian.write('NCT - why do we sleep.md', '---
nodeTypeId: pk-2176-no-content
---
A note whose type has no {content}.
'); })()

prepare.why: a plain note named in the Draft Claim format, not yet a node, for Bulk identify to find

apply.js: proof.obsidian.write('Claim (draft) - Coffee helps focus.md', 'A plain note, not a node yet.\n')

cases.title: The Content line extracts the content from a format with parentheses
cases.caption: In Obsidian, the Draft Claim format has parentheses too. The discourse context now reads the content, Sleep improves memory, instead of the word inside the parentheses.

steps.why: show the discourse context, if it isn't open

expect.js: proof.waitFor(() => { const view = document.querySelector('[data-type="discourse-context-view"]'); return view && /Content:\s*Sleep improves memory/.test(view.innerText); }, { what: 'Content: Sleep improves memory in the discourse context' })

cases.proves: Done When 1: `Claim (draft) - {content}` matches its titles and extracts `content` in both apps.

cases.title: Obsidian: Create discourse node names a Draft Claim note from the format, and its Content line reads the content

steps.why: create a node the way a user would

do.js: (() => { const select = document.querySelector('.modal select'); const setter = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLSelectElement.prototype, 'value').set; setter.call(select, 'pk-2176-draft-claim'); select.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true })); })()

(async () => { const file = await proof.waitFor(() => window.app.vault.getMarkdownFiles().find((f) => f.basename === 'Claim (draft) - Sleep improves memory consolidation'), { what: 'the new Draft Claim note', timeout: 15000 }); await proof.obsidian.open(file.path); })()

steps.why: show the discourse context, if it isn't open

cases.proves: Done When 1: `Claim (draft) - {content}` matches its titles and extracts `content` in both apps.

expect.js: proof.waitFor(() => { const view = document.querySelector('[data-type="discourse-context-view"]'); const match = view && /Content:\s*([^\n]+)/.exec(view.innerText); return match && match[1].trim() === "Sleep improves memory consolidation"; }, { what: "Content: Sleep improves memory consolidation for the new note" })

cases.checks: The new note is `Claim (draft) - Sleep improves memory consolidation`, and its discourse context reads Content: Sleep improves memory consolidation.
cases.caption: Creating a Draft Claim from the command names the note from the format with the parentheses, and its discourse context reads just the content.

cases.title: Obsidian publishes the same content its Content line shows

steps.why: start without a dialog or old notices

do.js: proof.waitFor(() => /synced successfully|Sync failed/.test(proof.obsidian.notices()), { what: 'the sync to finish', timeout: 120000, interval: 500 })

steps.why: show the discourse context, if it isn't open

cases.proves: Done When 2: One shared, unit-tested implementation of builder + extractor (at minimum: scan and builder share one grammar constant per app), and `DiscourseContextView` renders the same content string the converter publishes.

expect.js: (async () => { proof.assert(!/Sync failed/.test(proof.obsidian.notices()), 'Sync failed: ' + proof.obsidian.notices()); const shown = await proof.waitFor(() => { const view = document.querySelector('[data-type="discourse-context-view"]'); const match = view && /Content:\s*([^\n]+)/.exec(view.innerText); return match && match[1].trim(); }, { what: 'the Content line' }); const row = await proof.waitFor(async () => (await proof.rest('/rest/v1/Concept?select=literal_content&is_schema=eq.false&space_id=eq.106039&source_local_id=eq.pk-2176-draft-claim-note', { key: '{{env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY}}' }))[0], { what: 'the synced Draft Claim concept', timeout: 30000, interval: 1000 }); proof.assert(row.literal_content.core_title === shown, 'The Content line reads ' + JSON.stringify(shown) + ' but the published core_title is ' + JSON.stringify(row.literal_content.core_title) + '.'); proof.assert(shown === 'Sleep improves memory', 'Both read ' + JSON.stringify(shown) + '.'); })()

cases.checks: After Sync discourse nodes to Supabase, the Draft Claim note's published core_title equals its Content line, Sleep improves memory.
cases.caption: Sync the vault, and the Draft Claim note publishes exactly what its discourse context shows: Sleep improves memory.

show the discourse context, if it isn't open

cases.proves: The PR's declared behavior change, not tied to a bullet: a format with placeholders but no {content}, which only import can create, now yields the whole title.

expect.js: proof.waitFor(() => { const view = document.querySelector('[data-type="discourse-context-view"]'); const match = view && /Content:\s*([^\n]+)/.exec(view.innerText); return match && match[1].trim() === "NCT - why do we sleep"; }, { what: "Content: NCT - why do we sleep" })
expect.text: Content shows the whole title, NCT - why do we sleep. Before this PR it showed why do we sleep. This is the PR's open scope decision.

steps.why: open Bulk identify the way a user would

do.js: (async () => { const row = await proof.waitFor(() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.modal div.cursor-pointer')).find((div) => div.innerText.trim() === 'Draft Claim'), { what: 'the Draft Claim pattern' }); if (!row.querySelector('input[type=checkbox]').checked) row.click(); })()

expect.js: proof.waitFor(() => { const modal = document.querySelector('.modal'); return modal && modal.innerText.includes('Claim (draft) - Coffee helps focus'); }, { what: 'the plain Draft Claim note among the candidates' })

cases.title: Obsidian: create a parenthesised node from the command
cases.intent: In Obsidian, add a node type with format `Claim (draft) - {content}`. Select text and use Create discourse node, or run the command, then open the new note and the Discourse Context pane.

expect.text: The note is created with title `Claim (draft) - <text>`, is recognised as that type, and the context pane shows the node without errors.

decision.reason: obsidian-content-line already creates the note with Create discourse node and checks its name and Content line

claim: In Obsidian, a node format with parentheses matches its own notes and yields its content, the discourse context shows the same content the converter publishes, and ordinary formats behave as before.
given: Sid-Obsidian-test runs the ENG-2176 build, signed in to the proof database with sync mode on. It has a Draft Claim type (`Claim (draft) - {content}`) and a note in it, a default Claim note, a type whose format has no {content} and a note in it, and a plain note named in the Draft Claim format.

surface.area: Obsidian node creation and Discourse Context view
surface.why: createNode, the context pane, and QueryEngine import now use the shared builder and extractor instead of the old Obsidian copies.
